summary.headline: Eveready Q1 FY27 revenue rose 9% to INR407.7 crore with EBITDA margin of 15.1% and PAT up 22.3%, driven by alkaline batteries and price actions.
summary.overview: Q1 FY27 revenue was INR407.7 crore, up 9% YoY, marking the seventh consecutive quarter of YoY revenue growth. EBITDA was INR61.5 crore at a 15.1% margin and PAT was INR37 crore, up 22.3%. Management attributed margin protection to calibrated price increases and operational efficiencies, and stated there were no one-off gains. The Jammu alkaline plant began commercial production on 29 May 2026, while flashlights were soft on delayed monsoon and the lighting business reached breakeven.

segments.name: Batteries - Alkaline
segments.commentary: Key growth driver with close to 48% volume growth; premium alkaline market share reached 18%, with management targeting an exit share of 25-30% in two years. Alkaline is about 6-7% of company portfolio.

segments.name: Batteries - Carbon zinc
segments.commentary: Volume growth in line with industry (zinc market volumes roughly flat, -1% to +1%); company holds about 58% share of carbon zinc, described as broadly flattish. Legacy manufacturing costs reduced.

segments.name: Flashlights
segments.commentary: Revenue down 6.7% on delayed monsoon and lower conventional battery-operated volumes; rechargeable flashlights grew over 20%.

segments.name: Lighting
segments.commentary: Revenue up 13.7%; pricing stabilising after 18-20 months of erosion; company says segment broke even in Q1, with emergency LED bulbs and electrical accessories growing.

segments.name: Electrical accessories / wires
segments.commentary: Insulation tapes growing; wires and MCBs started about 6 months ago, with plans to more than double sales in FY27. Wires are sourced, not manufactured.

guidance_outlook: Management expects roughly 10% gross margin uplift on alkaline products from Jammu plant once fully stabilised (after about one year); operating margin not guided.
Alkaline market share target of 25-30% exit share in two years.
Debt expected to turn positive/like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters.
Lighting expected to grow in Q2 and Q3 FY27, with cost softening uncertain.
Management said another round of price or margin corrections may be needed to manage zinc inflation.
Long-term plan and M&A strategy to be presented in 2-3 quarters.
capex_capacity: Jammu alkaline plant commenced commercial production on 29 May 2026; company describes it as the only alkaline battery plant in India.
Jammu plant plant and machinery investment about INR90-95 crore; total Jammu investment INR200 crore-plus, yet to yield results.
Pre-operating expenses of Jammu plant capitalised; expenses after 29 May charged to P&L.
Jammu GST/incentive approval (NCSS scheme, 3x eligible plant and machinery refund over 10 years) still pending formal approval.
Noida plant closed and sold; one plot executed, second expected to close shortly. CCI matter: next hearing around late September 2026.
Solar power installed at Jammu and other plants; company moving toward leasing/rental model for assets.
demand_pricing: Zinc prices around $3,500/ton versus below $3,000 for most of last year; electrolytic manganese dioxide, electrodes, acetylene black and lighting components also inflated.
Alkaline market about INR550 crore (within a battery market of about INR4,100 crore at MRP); alkaline volume growth +19% to +23% over last 7-8 quarters, versus zinc flat.
Alkaline share of dry cell about 13-15%; Duracell is the largest alkaline competitor, Panasonic and Nippo are close followers in zinc.
Digital channels (quick commerce, e-commerce) showed strong growth.
Employee cost up only 2-3% YoY, reflecting the Noida closure.
Management flagged no immediate cannibalisation of zinc by alkaline; may emerge when alkaline exceeds about 20% of the battery market.

qa_highlights.question: Share gains in dry cell (58%) and whether Amazon Basics entry or BIS/EPR compliance is a risk.
qa_highlights.answer: 58% share refers to carbon zinc only. BIS on flashlights is on paper complete, with compliance to be driven across unbranded players over 2-3 quarters. EPR pricing and compliance are under discussion with MoEFCC and the Pollution Control Board, and no cost estimate was given.

qa_highlights.question: What operating margin will Jammu alkaline deliver versus imports?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 10% gross margin uplift on the product once stabilised, not operating margin. Alkaline is 6-7% of revenue, so the impact is modest for now.

qa_highlights.question: Is there an one-off in the margin, and how is zinc hedged?
qa_highlights.answer: No one-offs; margin came from calibrated price actions. Zinc is monitored weekly and further price or margin corrections may be needed.

qa_highlights.question: Consultancy fees to a director and timing of the GST subsidy.
qa_highlights.answer: NRC and Board approved a whole-time director's compensation; quantum not disclosed. GST incentive has no formal approval yet, with discussions advancing.

qa_highlights.question: When can the company be debt free and what is the Jammu fixed cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Debt around INR165 crore; company expects to be like-to-like debt free in 4-5 quarters. Jammu costs are absorbed into product cost, not separately disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Size of CCI matter and potential cash outgo.
qa_highlights.answer: Management cannot estimate the outcome; next hearing is in late September.

risks_watch: Zinc and commodity inflation; possible further price hikes could affect volumes.
Unresolved EPR compliance cost and pricing framework.
CCI matter with a potential INR150 crore outgo flagged by an analyst; management could not estimate it.
Pending GST incentive approval for Jammu.
Monsoon-dependent flashlight demand and structural decline in conventional flashlights.
Lighting margins at breakeven and dependent on price stability.
Emerging cannibalisation of carbon zinc by alkaline once alkaline crosses about 20% of the market.
summary.management_tone: Confident on growth and profitability, but cautious on zinc costs and regulatory items. Management was evasive on the Jammu operating margin, the director remuneration quantum, the CCI cash outgo and EPR costs, and deferred long-term targets by 2-3 quarters.
key_quotes: Our alkaline battery portfolio continued to be the key growth driver, delivering close to 48% volume growth during the quarter.

And as a result, our understanding of immediate cannibalization may not be correct because only at the saturation of some of these high-drain device demand is where there might be a cannibalistic impact.
